Create and Plot Strange Attractors

Source: R/attractor-package.R
attractor-package.Rd

Julien C. Sprott's book Strange Attractors: Creating Patterns in Chaos (1993) shows how to make an endless variety of fractal patterns from simple equations. You don't pick the coefficients yourself. The computer picks them at random, iterates the equations, and keeps the result only if the orbit settles into something worth looking at. The book describes over 350 such patterns, in two, three and more dimensions.

Details

This package implements only the example in chapter 7e. Give it a seed and it finds the coefficients for that seed, so the same seed always gives you the same picture. Then it iterates the map for as many points as you ask for.

The package is fast, because the iteration runs in Rust, and the points are binned (discretised) into a much smaller matrix, so plotting is cheap too.

Get started:

  • attractor_sprott_7e()

References

Sprott, J. C. (1993). Strange Attractors: Creating Patterns in Chaos. M&T Books, New York. Free PDF at https://sprott.physics.wisc.edu/fractals.htm.
